questions.question: Arihant starts doing a certain work. After 4 days, Arun who is half efficient as Arihant starts working on the same work. As a result, the work gets completed in 9 more days. What is the time to complete the work if Arun does it alone?
questions.questionHtml: Arihant starts doing a certain work. After 4 days, Arun who is half efficient as Arihant starts working on the same work. As a result, the work gets completed in 9 more days. What is the time to complete the work if Arun does it alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio of Arihant : Arun = 2 : 1 (since Arun is half efficient).

Total work = (Arihant total days × efficiency) + (Arun total days × efficiency)

Total work = (13 × 2) + (9 × 1) = 26 + 9 = 35 units.

Time for Arun alone = 35 units ÷ 1 unit/day = 35 days.

∴ The correct answer is 35 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Arihant worked for 4 days alone + 9 days with Arun = 13 days.

⇒ Arun worked for 9 days total.

⇒ Efficiency of Arun = 1/2 of Arihant efficiency.

Formula Used:

⇒ Total Work = (Efficiency × Time)

⇒ Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

Calculations:

⇒ Let Arun efficiency = 1 unit/day, then Arihant efficiency = 2 units/day.

Person Total Days Worked Efficiency Work Done (Units)
Arihant 13 2 26
Arun 9 1 9
Total Work - - 35

⇒ Total work performed = 26 + 9 = 35 units.

⇒ Time taken by Arun alone = Total Work ÷ Arun efficiency

⇒ Time = 35 ÷ 1 = 35 days.

∴ The correct answer is 35 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency-Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If efficiency ratio is a : b, the time ratio is b : a.

Combined Work Rule

When individuals work together, their daily efficiencies are added (Etotal = E1 + E2 + ... + En) to find the total rate of work.

Work Constant Formula

For the same piece of work, M1 × D1 × E1 = M2 × D2 × E2, where M is number of workers, D is days, and E is efficiency.

questions.question: 'A person bought shares worth ₹ 25 from a company. This company gives a dividend of 9%. If that person gets 10% income on his cost, then at what price should he buy the shares per share?
questions.questionHtml: 'A person bought shares worth ₹ 25 from a company. This company gives a dividend of 9%. If that person gets 10% income on his cost, then at what price should he buy the shares per share?
questions.solution:
Explanation -

A person bought shares worth ₹ 25 from a company. This company gives a dividend of 9%.

So dividend = 9% of ₹ 25  = 0.09 x 25 = ₹ 2.25

Now let the cost be x then according to the question -

10% of x = dividend

10% of x = ₹ 2.25

\(\frac{1}{10} \times x = 2.25 \implies x = 22.5\)

Hence the price is ₹ 22.5

questions.question: Jitin's age 3 years from now will be double the average of Jitin's current age and his age 8 years ago. What was Jitin's age 5 years ago?
questions.questionHtml: Jitin's age 3 years from now will be double the average of Jitin's current age and his age 8 years ago. What was Jitin's age 5 years ago?
questions.solution:
The average of Jitin's current age and his age 8 years ago is:

(a + (a - 8))/2 = (2a - 8)/2 = a - 4

a + 3 = 2(a - 4)  ⇒ 11 = a

Jitin's age 5 years ago is 11 - 5 = 6.

questions.question: A train 100 metres long, moving at a speed of 50 km per hour, crosses another train 120 metres long coming from the opposite direction in 6 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.questionHtml: A train 100 metres long, moving at a speed of 50 km per hour, crosses another train 120 metres long coming from the opposite direction in 6 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
Speed = Distance/time

A.T.Q. (100 + 120) m  = (50 + V) x 6 sec ⇒ 220 m = (50 + V) x 6 sec

⇒ \(\frac{220}{1000}\) km = (50 + V) x (\(\frac{6}{3600}\)) hr ⇒ 22 = (50 + V) x \(\frac{1}{6}\) 

⇒ V = 82 kmph

questions.question: The inner and outer diameter of a cylindrical pipe is 14 cm and 16 cm respectively. Find the weight of 7 cm long pipe, if the density of the metal used to make the pipe is 7.8 gm / cm 3
questions.questionHtml: The inner and outer diameter of a cylindrical pipe is 14 cm and 16 cm respectively. Find the weight of 7 cm long pipe, if the density of the metal used to make the pipe is 7.8 gm / cm<sup>3</sup>
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of hollow cylinder = π × (R2 − r2) × h

Inner radius (r) = 7 cm, Outer radius (R) = 8 cm, height (h) = 7 cm

Volume = (22/7) × (82 − 72) × 7 = 22 × (64 − 49) = 22 × 15 = 330 cm3

Weight = Volume × Density = 330 × 7.8 = 2574 gm = 2.574 kg

∴ The correct answer is 2.574 kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Inner diameter = 14 cm ⇒ Inner radius (r) = 7 cm

Outer diameter = 16 cm ⇒ Outer radius (R) = 8 cm

Length (h) = 7 cm

Density = 7.8 gm/cm3

Formula Used:

Volume of material = π × (R2 − r2) × h

Weight = Volume × Density

Calculations:

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (82 − 72) × 7

⇒ Volume = 22 × (64 − 49)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 15 = 330 cm3

⇒ Weight in gm = 330 × 7.8

⇒ Weight in gm = 2574 gm

⇒ Weight in kg = 2574 / 1000 = 2.574 kg

∴ The correct answer is 2.574 kg.

Additional Information

Hollow Cylinder Surface Area

Total Surface Area = 2πR h + 2πr h + 2π(R2 − r2). This includes inner, outer, and base areas.

Density Conversion

1 gm/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3. To convert grams to kilograms, divide the value by 1000.

Volume of Solid Cylinder

The volume of a solid cylinder is given by πr2h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of a circle = 12 cm

Formula used:

Area of square = side × side

Diagonal of square = √2 × side

Calculations:

According to problem,

Diagonal of square = 2 × radius of a circle

=> √2 × side = 2 × 12

=> side = 12√2 cm 

Required area of square = 12√2 × 12√2

= 144 × 2

= 288 sq.cm.

∴ The answer is 288 sq.cm.

questions.question: Population of Town A is 30% more than the population of town B. The population of town C is 40% more than the population of town A. The difference between the population of town B and C is 172200. Find the population of town A?
questions.questionHtml: Population of Town A is 30% more than the population of town B. The population of town C is 40% more than the population of town A. The difference between the population of town B and C is 172200. Find the population of town A?
questions.solution:
Given that,

A’s population = 130/100 × B’s population

A : B = 13 : 10

C’s population = 140/100 × A’s population

C : A = 14 : 10

Combined ratio = A : B : C

⇒ 65 : 50 : 91

Difference between B and C’s population = 172200

⇒ (91 – 50) units = 172200

1 unit = 4200

∴ A’s population = 4200 × 65 = 273000

questions.question: LCM of two prime numbers x and y (x > y) is 253. The difference between the numbers x and y is:
questions.questionHtml: LCM of two prime numbers x and y (x > y) is 253. The difference between the numbers x and y is:
questions.solution:
Given:

LCM of x and y = 253

Also, x > y

Concept used:

HCF of two prime numbers is always 1

Calculation:

We know that HCF of x and y = 1

x × y = 1 × 253 = 253

Now by prime factorizing the number we get

253 = 11 × 23

∴ The numbers are 11 and 23

Difference between numbers = 23 - 11 = 12

∴ The difference between the numbers x and y is 12.

questions.question: The value of (1 + cot θ - cosec θ) (1 + tan θ + sec θ) is ________ ?
questions.questionHtml: The value of (1 + cot θ - cosec θ) (1 + tan θ + sec θ) is ________?
questions.solution:
Given

(1 + cot θ - cosec θ) (1 + tan θ + sec θ)

Solution

⇒ (1 + cosθ/sinθ - 1/sinθ) (1 + sinθ/cosθ + 1/cosθ)

⇒ {(sinθ + cosθ - 1)/sinθ} × {cosθ + sinθ + 1)/cosθ   ∵ (a + b) (a - b) = a2 - b2

⇒ {(sinθ + cosθ)2 - 1}/sinθ × cosθ 

⇒ (sin2θ + cos2θ + 2sinθ × cosθ  - 1)/sinθ × cosθ 

SInce, sin2θ + cos2θ  = 1,

⇒ (1 + 2sinθ × cosθ  - 1)/sinθ × cosθ 

⇒ 2sinθ × cosθ /sinθ × cosθ 

⇒ 2.

questions.question: Pinki and Rinki together can do a piece of work in 20 days. Rinki and Minki together can do it in 12 days while Pinki and Minki together can do it in 15 days. In how long can Rinki alone do it?
questions.questionHtml: Pinki and Rinki together can do a piece of work in 20 days. Rinki and Minki together can do it in 12 days while Pinki and Minki together can do it in 15 days. In how long can Rinki alone do it?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work = LCM(20, 12, 15) = 60 units.

Efficiency: (Pinki+Rinki) = 3, (Rinki+Minki) = 5, (Pinki+Minki) = 4.

2 × (Pinki+Rinki+Minki) efficiency = 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 ⇒ P+R+M = 6 units/day.

Rinki efficiency = (P+R+M) − (Pinki+Minki) = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day.

Time for Rinki = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days.

∴ The correct answer is 30 day.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (Pinki + Rinki) = 20 days

Time taken by (Rinki + Minki) = 12 days

Time taken by (Pinki + Minki) = 15 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

Persons Time Total Work Efficiency
Pinki + Rinki 20
60
 3
Rinki + Minki 12 5
Pinki + Minki 15 4

Combined efficiency of 2 × (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) = 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 units/day

Calculations:

⇒ Total efficiency of (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Rinki = Efficiency of (Pinki + Rinki + Minki) − Efficiency of (Pinki + Minki)

⇒ Efficiency of Rinki = 6 − 4 = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Rinki alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Rinki

⇒ Time taken by Rinki alone = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days

∴ The correct answer is 30 day.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If a person takes T days to complete work, their efficiency is 1/T units per day.

Combined Work Formula

When pairs are given, the total efficiency 2 × (A+B+C) = Eff(A+B) + Eff(B+C) + Eff(C+A). Individual efficiency is found by subtracting the pair that does not include the target person.

Work and Wages

In any piece of work, wages are always distributed in the ratio of the amount of work done by each individual, which depends on their efficiency and time spent working.

questions.question: The compound interest (compounding half yearly) received on Rs. 10000 for 1.5 years is Rs. 3676.31. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest (compounding half yearly) received on Rs. 10000 for 1.5 years is Rs. 3676.31. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal (P) = ₹10,000

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹3,676.31

Time (t) = 1.5 years

Interest is compounded half-yearly.

Formula used:

Compound Interest (CI) = P × [(1 + r/n)nt - 1]

Where,

P = Principal

r = annual rate of interest (in decimal)

n = number of times the interest is compounded per year (n = 2 for half-yearly)

t = time in years

Calculation:

We know that CI = ₹3,676.31, so:

₹3,676.31 = ₹10,000 × [(1 + r/2)2 × 1.5 - 1]

⇒ ₹3,676.31 = ₹10,000 × [(1 + r/2)3 - 1]

⇒ 0.367631 = (1 + r/2)3 - 1

⇒ (1 + r/2)3 = 1.367631

Taking the cube root of both sides:

1 + r/2 = (1.367631)1/3

1 + r/2 = 1.11

⇒ r/2 = 1.11 - 1 = 0.11

⇒ r = 0.22 = 22%

Therefore, the rate of interest per annum is 22%.

questions.question: In what ratio, rice costing Rs. 185 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 95 per kg such that by selling the mixture at Rs. 140 per kg there is a gain of 40%?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio, rice costing Rs. 185 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 95 per kg such that by selling the mixture at Rs. 140 per kg there is a gain of 40%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Mean Cost Price = 140 ÷ 1.4 = Rs. 100

Ratio = (Mean CP − Cheaper CP) : (Dearer CP − Mean CP)

Ratio = (100 − 95) : (185 − 100)

Ratio = 5 : 85 = 1 : 17

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 17.

Alternate Method

Given: CP1 = Rs. 185/kg, CP2 = Rs. 95/kg, SPmix = Rs. 140/kg, Profit = 40%

Formula Used: CP = [SP × 100] / [100 + Profit %]

⇒ Cost Price of mixture = 140 × [100 / (100 + 40)]

⇒ Mean CP = 140 × (100 / 140) = Rs. 100

⇒ By Alligation Rule: Ratio = (100 − 95) : (185 − 100)

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 85

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 17

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 17.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It states that (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (CP of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − CP of Cheaper).

Cost Price Calculation

When selling price and profit percentage are given, CP = SP / (1 + P%), where P% is the profit expressed as a decimal.

Multiple Mixtures

The alligation method can be extended to three or more ingredients by grouping them in pairs based on the mean price.

questions.question: If m and n are the two digits of the number 1798mn such that this number is divisible by 70, then (m + n) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If m and n are the two digits of the number 1798mn such that this number is divisible by 70, then (m + n) is equal to:
questions.solution:
For 1798mn to be divisible by 70:

Divisible by 10 ⇒ n = 0. Number is 1798m0.

Divisible by 7 ⇒ 1798 - 2m is divisible by 7.

1798 mod 7 = 6.

So, 6 - 2m ≡ 0 (mod 7).

Testing digits, m = 3 works (6 - 6 = 0).

Therefore, m + n = 3 + 0 = 3.

questions.question: Alpha and Beta invested their capital in the ratio of 17 ∶ 15 in a partnership. At the end of 17 months, Beta withdraws his capital. If they share profit in the ratio of 4 ∶ 3, then for how many months Alpha invested his capital?
questions.questionHtml: Alpha and Beta invested their capital in the ratio of 17 ∶ 15 in a partnership. At the end of 17 months, Beta withdraws his capital. If they share profit in the ratio of 4 ∶ 3, then for how many months Alpha invested his capital?
questions.solution:
Ratio of profit of partners = Ratio of their investments.

Let Alpha invested for x months.

Ratio of profit of Alpha ∶ Beta = x × 17 ∶ 17 × 15

So, 4 ∶ 3 = 17x ∶ 17 × 15 ⇒ 17x = (4 × 17 × 15)/3 ⇒ x = 20

questions.questionHtml: The average income of 30 persons is Rs. 5,600 and that of another 25 persons is Rs. 5,000. Find the average income of the whole group.

= \(\dfrac{30\times 5600 + 25 \times 5000 }{30 + 25}\) = 5327.27.

questions.question: ​ If points (a, 0), (0, b) and (1, 1) are collinear then what is the value of (a + b)
questions.questionHtml: ​If points (a, 0), (0, b) and (1, 1) are collinear then what is the value of (a + b)
questions.solution:
Let (x1, y1) = (a, 0), (x2, y2) = (0, b) and (x3, y3) = (1, 1)

Condition for three points to be collinear is; 

x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2) = 0

⇒ a (b - 1) + 0 (1 - 0) + 1 (0 - b) = 0 ⇒ ab - a - b = 0 ⇒ a + b = ab

questions.question: The area of a rectangle whose length is 5 units more than twice its width is 75 square units. What is its width?
questions.questionHtml: The area of a rectangle whose length is 5 units more than twice its width is 75 square units. What is its width?
questions.solution:
Length = (2x + 5) units

⇒ (2x + 5) x = 75 ⇒ 2x2 + 5x - 75 = 0

⇒ 2x2 + 15x - 10x - 75 = 0 ⇒ x (2x + 15) - 5 (2x + 15) = 0

⇒ (x - 5) (2x + 15) ⇒ x = 5, -15/2 (neglecting negative value) ∴ Width of Rectangle is equal to 5 units.

questions.question: The perimeter of one square is 52 metre and that of another is 20 metre. What is the perimeter of the square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of the two squares?
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of one square is 52 metre and that of another is 20 metre. What is the perimeter of the square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of the two squares?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Side of first square = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 m

Side of second square = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m

Using Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13): 132 − 52 = 122

Side of the required square = 12 m

Required Perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 m

∴ The correct option is D.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of Square1 = 52 m

Perimeter of Square2 = 20 m

Formula Used:

Perimeter of square = 4 × side

Area of square = side2

1 Side = 13m − Area2 Side = 5m = Area3 Side = 12m

Calculations:

⇒ Side of Square1 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 m

⇒ Area of Square1 = 132 = 169 m2

⇒ Side of Square2 = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m

⇒ Area of Square2 = 52 = 25 m2

⇒ Area of Square3 = Area1 − Area2

⇒ Area of Square3 = 169 − 25 = 144 m2

⇒ Side of Square3 = √144 = 12 m

⇒ Perimeter of Square3 = 4 × 12 = 48 m

∴ The correct option is D.

Additional Information

Area of Square

The area of a square is calculated by squaring its side length (Area = side × side). If area is known, side = √Area.

Perimeter of Square

The perimeter is the total length of the boundary, calculated as 4 × side. If perimeter is known, side = Perimeter ÷ 4.

Pythagorean Triplets in Mensuration

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) are often used to relate sides of squares when their areas are added or subtracted.

questions.question: x varies inversely as y. When x = 3.5, then y = 2.4. What is the value of y when x = 5.6?
questions.questionHtml: x varies inversely as y. When x = 3.5, then y = 2.4. What is the value of y when x = 5.6?
questions.solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the concept of inverse variation, which states that when two variables x and y vary inversely, their product remains constant. Mathematically, this can be represented as xy = k

For x = 3.5 and y = 2.4, xy = 8.4

When x = 5.6, 5.6 × y = 8.4 ⇒ y = 8.4/5.6 ⇒ y = 1.5

questions.question: What is the probability that in a family of 4 children, there will be at least one boy?
questions.questionHtml: What is the probability that in a family of 4 children, there will be at least one boy?
questions.solution:
Each child has two possibilities, boy or girl.

Let B: boy and G: girl

Then possible outcomes = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16

If there is no boy then 4 children are girls so

The probability to have no boy = \(\frac{1}{16}\)

⇒ Probability to have at least one boy = 1 − \(\frac{1}{16}\) = \(\frac{15}{16}\)

questions.question: The variable L is in joint variation with M and N. When the values of M and N are 6 and 8, L is 32. What is the value of L when M = 10 and N = 15?
questions.questionHtml: The variable L is in joint variation with M and N. When the values of M and N are 6 and 8, L is 32. What is the value of L when M = 10 and N = 15?
questions.solution:
Given:

The variable L is in joint variation with M and N

When the values of M and N are 6 and 8, L is 32

Concept used:

if L is in joint variation with M and N it means L is directly proportional to M and N

L = K × M × N ( K is a constant in place of proportionality)

Calculation:

When the values of M and N are 6 and 8, L is 32

L = K × M × N ( K is a constant in place of proportionality)

32 =  K × 6 × 8

K = \(\frac{2}{3}\)

if M = 10 and N = 15,

L = K × M × N

= \(\frac{2}{3}\) × 10 × 15

= 2 × 10 × 5

= 100

The value of L is 100 when M = 10 and N = 15

Answer is 100.

questions.question: When the speed of a car is increased by 25%, it takes 24 minutes less to cover the same distance. What is the time (in hours) taken to cover the same distance at the actual speed?
questions.questionHtml: When the speed of a car is increased by 25%, it takes 24 minutes less to cover the same distance. What is the time (in hours) taken to cover the same distance at the actual speed?
questions.solution:
Given:

When the speed of a car is increased by 25%, it takes 24 minutes less to cover the same distance. 

Formula:

 Distance = Speed × Time

Concept used:

The speed ratio is inversely proportional to the time ratio.

Calculation:

Let, the speed of the car be 100 units

So after increased speed = (100 + 100 × 25/100) 

⇒ 100 + 25 = 125 units

So speed ratio is 100: 125 = 4: 5

So, the time ratio will be 5:4

Let, the time at 1st be 5x and then be 4x

As per the question 5x - 4x = 24 

⇒ x = 24 minutes 

So, initial time 

5x = 5 × 24

⇒ 120 minutes = 2hr

∴ The time  taken to cover the same distance at the actual speed is 2 hour

questions.question: (secA + tanA)(1 - sinA) = ?
questions.questionHtml: (secA + tanA)(1 - sinA) = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

(secA + tanA)(1 - sinA)

Concept used:

secA = (1/cosA)

tanA = sinA/cosA

Calculation:

(secA + tanA)(1 - sinA)

⇒ secA - sinA.secA + tanA - sinA.tanA

⇒ secA - sinA/cosA + tanA - sinA × (sinA/cosA)

⇒ secA - tanA + tanA - sin2A/cosA

⇒ secA - sin2A.secA

⇒ secA(1 - sin2A)

⇒ secA(cos2A)

⇒ cosA

∴ The required answer is cosA.

questions.question: Raghu bought an article for Rs. 6800 and spent Rs. 700 on its repairs. He marked this article at 8% above the overall cost price. He sold the article for Rs. 6,480 after giving x% discount. The value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: Raghu bought an article for Rs. 6800 and spent Rs. 700 on its repairs. He marked this article at 8% above the overall cost price. He sold the article for Rs. 6,480 after giving x% discount. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Raghu bought an article for Rs. 6800 and spent Rs. 700 on its repairs.

He marked this article at 8% above the overall cost price.

SP = Rs. 6,480

Formula used:

Discount = MP – SP

Discount% = Discount/MP × 100

Calculation:

Total CP = Rs. (6800 + 700) = Rs. 7500

He marked this article at 8% above the overall cost price.

⇒ (7,500 × 108/100)

⇒ MP = Rs. 8,100

Now,

Discount = MP – SP

⇒ Rs. (8100 – 6480)

⇒ Rs. 1620

Discount% = Discount/MP × 100

⇒ (1620/8100 × 100)

questions.question: By selling a cycle at a discount of 20%, the seller made a profit of 12%. If the cost price of the cycle is Rs. 5,000, then what was the marked price of the cycle?
questions.questionHtml: By selling a cycle at a discount of 20%, the seller made a profit of 12%. If the cost price of the cycle is Rs. 5,000, then what was the marked price of the cycle?
questions.solution:
Concept use:

SP = CP + Profit​

Selling price = Marked/List price – Discount

Calculations:

SP = CP + Profit
SP = 5000 + 0.12 × 5000 = Rs. 5600

The selling price after a discount of 20% means the marked price (MP) is 80% of the selling price.

SP = 0.80 ×  MP
5600 = 0.80 ×  MP
MP = 5600 / 0.80 = Rs. 7000

Hence, the marked price of the cycle is Rs. 7000

questions.solution:
Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2000

Rate (R) = 8% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculation:

SI = (2000 × 8 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (32000) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = ₹320

∴ The simple interest is ₹320.

questions.question: If 19 November 2005 is a Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 23 November 2008?
questions.questionHtml: If 19 November 2005 is a Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 23 November 2008?
questions.solution:
19 November 2005 is a Saturday.

Consider a regular year of days 365 as we know there are 52 weeks in a year. On consideration, each week has 7 days so there will total (52*7) = 364 days. That means if we started counting from Monday as 1st day then the 364th day will be Monday. The remaining day of the year will add up to the next day of the week from where we started, i.e., it will be Tuesday. That remaining day is called an odd day. 

A normal year has 1 odd day, whereas a leap year has 2 odd days.

So, 2006 = 1 odd day

2007 = 1 odd day

2008 = 2 odd day (Leap year)

Total number of odd days = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4

Saturday + 4 days = Wednesday.

19 November 2008 will be ‘Wednesday’.

Now in question we have asked about 23 November 2008

23 -19 = 4 (days)

Wednesday + 4 = Sunday

Hence, the correct answer is “Sunday”.

questions.question: The weight of three friends is in the ratio of 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 5. If the sum of their weights is 192 kg, find the weight of the lightest friend.
questions.questionHtml: The weight of three friends is in the ratio of 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 5. If the sum of their weights is 192 kg, find the weight of the lightest friend.
questions.solution:
Let the weight of the 3 friends be ‘4x’, ‘3x’ and ‘5x’.

Sum of weights = 4x + 3x + 5x = 12x

⇒ 12x = 192

⇒ x = 192/12 = 16

∴ Weight of the lightest friend = 3x = 3(16) = 48 kg

questions.question: Which of the two signs should be interchanged in order to make the following equation correct? 21 + 5 × 2 – 21 ÷ 3 = 12
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the two signs should be interchanged in order to make the following equation correct?

21 + 5 × 2 – 21 ÷ 3 = 12
questions.solution:
Given Equation: 21 + 5 × 2 – 21 ÷ 3 = 12

1) + and -

After interchanging signs

LHS = 21 - 5 × 2 + 21 ÷ 3 = 21 – 10 + 7 = 18 ≠ RHS

2) – and ÷

After interchanging signs

LHS = 21 + 5 × 2 ÷ 21 – 3 = 21 + 0.476 – 3 = 18. 476 ≠ RHS

3) – and ×

After interchanging signs

LHS = 21 + 5 - 2 × 21 ÷ 3 = 21 + 5 – 14 = 12 = RHS

4) × and ÷

After interchanging signs

LHS = 21 + 5 ÷ 2 – 21 × 3 = 21 + 2.5 – 63 = - 39.5 ≠ RHS

Hence, “– and ×” is the correct answer.
